reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a tutorial about contacting Facebook customer care and addressing a missing support button. The described feedback form and 24-hour response are presented as a support-contact procedure, with no stated request for sensitive information or payment. The separate subscribe prompt is ordinary channel engagement and is not connected to a financial or credential-related offer.

citations.quote: So what procedure do you have to follow if you're watching this video for the first time?
So you have to fill out this feedback form, you submit it to Facebook
if they don't have the button for gate support
Bahot Sare Logo Ko Problem Hota Hai Facebook Ko Kaise Contact Kare.

opening.argument: The video ties a concrete promised outcome to a low-effort viewer action: submit a feedback form and receive an answer and solution within 24 hours. That is more than general discussion; it presents the submission as the route to obtaining help for an account problem. The promise is broad, covering “whatever problem you have,” while the material does not establish that the form will actually deliver the claimed result. That combination of an easy action and a specific promised outcome supports treating the procedure as a scam-like acquisition flow rather than a neutral explanation.

citations.quote: So you have to fill out this feedback form, you submit it to Facebook, and within 24 hours

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the form a support procedure does not resolve the central concern: viewers are instructed to submit information in exchange for a promised answer and solution within a fixed time. The cited material establishes the action and the promised result, but it does not establish that the promise is reliable or that the form is an official Facebook process. The absence of an explicit payment demand does not eliminate a deceptive support-recovery pathway.

citations.quote: within 24 hours, Facebook will give you the answer to whatever problem you have
Facebook feedback form:- https://www.facebook.com/help/Contact/268228888883256323

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted passage describes assistance, not a reward, asset, withdrawal, or payment. It says viewers should submit a feedback form to Facebook, and the supplied description identifies the destination as a Facebook help URL. The promise of an answer or solution does not show that viewers obtain something of value through a scam mechanism, and nothing in the evidence shows credential harvesting or a non-Facebook destination.

citations.quote: So you have to fill out this feedback form, you submit it to Facebook
Facebook feedback form:- https://www.facebook.com/help/Contact/268228888883256323

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external link is supplied, the viewer is directed to submit a form, and the video promises a response and solution within 24 hours. The surrounding problem context is also high-stakes, referring to hacked Facebook accounts and pages and to people who cannot contact Facebook. Those conditions make viewers unusually receptive to an easy recovery route. A fast, broadly worded resolution promise attached to a link and submission request is precisely the kind of presentation that can make a questionable support flow look dependable.

citations.quote: Facebook feedback form:- https://www.facebook.com/help/Contact/268228888883256323
bahot sare hacker apke Facebook account or page Account ko recover kare
within 24 hours, Facebook will give you the answer to whatever problem you have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that an address is presented as a link does not make it trustworthy, and the promise is unusually sweeping: it covers whatever problem the viewer has and gives a 24-hour expectation. The reference characterization focuses on what is not explicitly requested, but a scam can use an apparently helpful recovery form without mentioning payment or passwords in the spoken excerpt. The combination of urgency, account vulnerability, and submission is still materially suspicious.

citations.quote: within 24 hours
Bahot Sare Logo Ko Problem Hota Hai Facebook Ko Kaise Contact Kare.
Facebook support can't access my Account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are contextual concerns, not evidence of a scam category. The description explicitly frames the subject as contacting Facebook, and the supplied URL is shown as a Facebook help URL. The evidence contains no payment, investment, reward, asset, credential request, or non-Facebook redirect. A 24-hour service expectation may be overconfident, but it does not turn an operational support tutorial into a reward-acquisition scam.

citations.quote: How to Contact Facebook Customer Care | Facebook Get Support Button Issue Solved
Facebook feedback form:- https://www.facebook.com/help/Contact/268228888883256323

opening.argument: Although the material adopts an instructional tone, it also steers viewers toward participation. The speaker repeatedly frames the form as the route to resolving account problems, while the sampled visuals place “Get Support Button Issue” beside a prominent “Subscribe” prompt. This makes the content function as promotion for a support-contact pathway and for the channel, not merely detached education. Viewers facing account trouble are encouraged to act on the presented route because it is associated with a promised solution, creating a low-friction funnel around a claimed benefit.

citations.quote: So you have to fill out this feedback form, you submit it to Facebook
it will give you the solution to whatever problem you have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional label does not answer the promotional mechanics. The speaker tells viewers what to submit and associates that action with a promised solution, while the frame visibly adds a subscription prompt. That combination shows steering toward participation and channel engagement, rather than simply explaining Facebook’s limitations. The defense also assumes the route is legitimate without evidence establishing that the claimed support outcome follows.

citations.quote: So you have to fill out this feedback form, you submit it to Facebook, and within 24 hours

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual only shows a generic subscription prompt alongside the issue title; it does not connect subscribing to a reward, payment, account recovery, or other asset. The spoken instruction directs viewers to submit a feedback form to Facebook, not to buy, deposit, recruit, or claim anything. Promotion of a channel or explanation of a support route is insufficient to establish the specified scam pattern.
